title: Refuse an unknown moduleId on POST /api/feature-matrix (parity with import)
body:
## Summary
POST /api/feature-matrix writes full upsert rows for any moduleId string; the import route now refuses ids outside SUB_MODULE_IDS (be772ed6), this sibling does not.

## Description
src/app/api/feature-matrix/route.ts:62 only checks `!moduleId`; `upsertFeatures(moduleId as SubModuleId, …)` at :87 then writes rows under any id. Two writers of one table, one guarded. Fixed = the same SUB_MODULE_IDS check as src/app/api/feature-matrix/import/route.ts. Not built this round because the seed callers (seedOnly batches) were not enumerated: a caller seeding a module id outside the enum would start getting 400.

## Flow
- enumerate every POST /api/feature-matrix caller (grep `/api/feature-matrix'` + `method: 'POST'`) and the moduleIds they send
- add a test: unknown moduleId -> 400, zero rows
- add the SUB_MODULE_IDS check after the non-object guard

## Expected impact
Stops garbage module rows that no view reads and that inflate scope reports. Could break a seed caller that uses a non-enum id - the enumeration step decides.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one closed module vocabulary across both feature_matrix writers
Before: POST {moduleId:"not-a-module", features:[complete row]} -> 200, 1 row (read of route.ts:62-87)
After: predicted 400, 0 rows
Method: simulation - not run: caller enumeration needed before landing
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test (unknown id -> 400, 0 rows) + caller grep proving no in-tree caller sends a non-enum id

title: feature-matrix/progress reports a thrown read as success {scanned:0,total:0}
body:
## Summary
The progress poll swallows every error into a success envelope that says the module has no features.

## Description
src/app/api/feature-matrix/progress/route.ts:57-59: the outer catch logs and returns `apiSuccess({ scanned: 0, total: 0 })`. `total: 0` is the same answer as "this module has no definitions" (:26-28), so a failing read (EACCES, a projectPath that is a file) is indistinguishable from an empty module and the review progress bar silently resets. Fixed = `apiError(msg, 500)` (the client poll already tolerates a failed poll) or a `{ measured: false, reason }` field.

## Flow
- GET /api/feature-matrix/progress?moduleId=arpg-combat&projectPath=<a path whose .pof/matrix/arpg-combat.json is a directory>
- readFileSync throws EISDIR inside the inner try -> regex fallback also throws -> scanned 0
- outer catch path: any other throw -> success {0,0}

## Expected impact
Operator watching a review sees "0 / 0" instead of a reason. Changing the envelope could make the poll hook show an error toast - check its handling.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed progress read says it failed
Before: 1 catch returns success with fabricated zeros (route.ts:57-59)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - read of the two catch paths; hook behaviour on a 500 not yet checked
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test forcing a throw (mock fs.existsSync to throw) asserting non-success, plus the poll hook test on a failed poll

title: Operator-guard the ability-spec writes (POST /api/ability-spec and /codegen)
body:
## Summary
ability_specs is catalog-pipeline source-of-record data keyed by catalogId/entityId, but both writers are unguarded while /api/catalog-entities (same keys) calls requireOperator.

## Description
src/app/api/ability-spec/route.ts:47 and src/app/api/ability-spec/codegen/route.ts:19 write SQLite with no `requireOperator`; src/app/api/catalog-entities/route.ts:112 guards the sibling write. The codegen route even says "the route is a public POST endpoint" (:31-32). A cross-site page can overwrite a spell's effects/tagRules (the GAS C++ codegen input). Fixed = `requireOperator(req)` first in both POSTs; the CLI callback is server-to-server with no Origin and keeps working.

## Flow
- cross-site POST text/plain {catalogId,entityId,effects:[],tagRules:[]} -> 200 today, stored spec wiped
- add requireOperator; test cross-site 403, header-less 200, token-less 401 when POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN set

## Expected impact
Closes a drive-by overwrite of authored GAS specs. Breaks any caller with a foreign Origin (none known).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - same guard on every catalog-keyed write
Before: 0/2 ability-spec writers guarded vs 1/1 catalog-entities writer
After: predicted 2/2
Method: simulation - grep of requireOperator usage; not run this round (budget)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Operator-guard the game-director writer seam (create/complete/ingest/triage)
body:
## Summary
POST /api/game-director is the external writer API (sessions stamped source:external) and is unguarded; a cross-site request can create sessions, complete them with fabricated summaries and route findings into the feature matrix.

## Description
src/app/api/game-director/route.ts:245 POST has no requireOperator; `complete` (:275) defaults provenance to external and runs completeSessionPipeline, which writes feature_matrix rows (routeFindingsToMatrix). DELETE (:429) deletes sessions. The house guards every route that writes the source of record (api-auth.ts docblock). Fixed = requireOperator on POST and DELETE.

## Flow
- cross-site POST {action:"create",...} then {action:"complete", summary:{...}} -> session stamped external + matrix rows updated
- add guard; test cross-site 403, same-origin 200

## Expected impact
Provenance "external" can no longer be forged by a drive-by page. Any foreign-Origin caller (none known in-tree) would break.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - provenance writes guarded like other source-of-record writes
Before: 0/2 write handlers guarded
After: predicted 2/2
Method: simulation - code read; not run (budget)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: operator-guard route test (cross-site 403 / same-origin 200 / token 401) over POST create and DELETE

title: Validate the combat scenario shape before the engine (playerGear/playerLevel -> 500)
body:
## Summary
POST /api/combat-simulator validates enemies but not playerGear/playerAbilities/playerLevel; a missing gear crashes the engine with a 500.

## Description
src/app/api/combat-simulator/route.ts:79-81 checks only `scenario.enemies`. Probe 2026-11-08: scenario without playerGear -> 500 "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'bonuses')"; playerLevel:"x" -> 500 "reading 'count'". Fixed = clamp playerLevel (clampInt like config) and require playerGear (object with bonuses) and playerAbilities (array) with 400s naming the field.

## Flow
- POST simulate with scenario {enemies:[valid]} only -> 500
- add field checks next to the enemies check
- test: each missing/wrong field -> 400 naming it; full scenario unchanged

## Expected impact
MCP/scripted callers get a fixable 400 instead of a retried 500. Store sends full scenarios, unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - caller errors classified at the boundary
Before: probe: 2/2 malformed scenarios -> 500
After: predicted 0/2 -> 500
Method: probe - before figure taken on the live route; fix not built (budget)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/app/api/combat-simulator/route.ts:79-81
probe: scenario w/o playerGear -> 500 bonuses; playerLevel "x" -> 500 count
instrument: route test with a minimal-enemies scenario and per-field mutations

title: economy-simulator generate-code trusts a client-supplied result object (500 / garbage C++)
body:
## Summary
action generate-code passes `body.result` straight into generateUE5Code; any non-SimulationResult crashes with a 500.

## Description
src/app/api/economy-simulator/route.ts:51-52 `if (body.result) simResult = body.result`. Probe 2026-11-08: result {} / {metrics:[]} / "x" -> 500 "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'philosophy')". The re-simulate branch was hardened (normalizeSimulationConfig) but this branch emits "calibrated" UE5 C++ from unchecked input. Fixed = re-simulate from `result.config` through normalizeSimulationConfig, or a shape check with a 400.

## Flow
- POST {action:"generate-code", result:{}} -> 500
- choose: shape-check (400) vs re-simulate from result.config
- test both

## Expected impact
Codegen can no longer emit C++ from a fabricated result. The UI sends a real result; unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - generated C++ only from validated simulation output
Before: probe: 3/3 malformed results -> 500
After: predicted 3/3 -> 400
Method: probe - before taken on the live route; fix not built
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test: malformed result -> 400; real result -> same codegen as today

title: game-director add-finding / add-event write unvalidated payloads (SQLite errors as 500)
body:
## Summary
add-finding and add-event cast the body to PlaytestFinding/DirectorEvent and hand it to SQL; a missing field or bad severity surfaces as a raw SQLite 500.

## Description
src/app/api/game-director/route.ts:298-302 and :335-339 do no checks; the findings table has CHECKs on severity/confidence_basis/triage_status (src/lib/game-director-db.ts:56-76) and NOT NULL columns, so a caller error is answered 500 with the SQLite message - the same class update-status had (fixed ca7d5a44). Also a finding for a non-existent sessionId is accepted. Fixed = a validator (sessionId exists, id string, severity in the closed set) returning 400/404.

## Flow
- POST {action:"add-finding", finding:{id:"f",sessionId:"x",severity:"huge"}} -> 500 CHECK constraint
- add validator; test 400 / 404 / valid 200

## Expected impact
External harnesses get actionable refusals. In-repo sim writes through the DB directly, unaffected.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - caller errors classified at the boundary
Before: 2 write actions with 0 field checks (route.ts:298-302, 335-339)
After: predicted 2 with checks
Method: simulation - code read + CHECK list; not probed
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test per action with bad severity / missing session / valid payload

title: ability-spec / balance-baseline persist array elements without a shape check
body:
## Summary
POST /api/ability-spec stores effects/tagRules/attributes elements of any shape; POST /api/balance-baseline stores any stats[] elements - garbage reaches the GAS codegen and the threat-score reader.

## Description
src/app/api/ability-spec/route.ts:57-64 checks only Array.isArray for effects/tagRules and optionalSlice (:13-18) only Array.isArray for slices; src/app/api/balance-baseline/route.ts:31-37 the same for stats. `effects:[1,"x",null]` is persisted and later fed to gas-codegen. Fixed = per-element minimal shape guards (object with the id/name field the consumer reads) with a 400 naming the index.

## Flow
- POST ability-spec {catalogId,entityId,effects:[null],tagRules:[]} -> 200, stored
- read back -> codegen consumer dereferences null
- add element guards + tests

## Expected impact
Stored specs stay readable by codegen. Risk: an over-strict guard refuses a legit legacy element - derive guards from the consumer reads.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - only consumable elements persisted
Before: 4 array fields with 0 element checks
After: predicted 4 with checks
Method: simulation - code read; consumer field set not yet enumerated
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route tests with null/primitive elements + a read-back through the codegen consumer

title: gdd-compliance takes projectPath/gapId/moduleId without type checks
body:
## Summary
POST /api/gdd-compliance passes body.projectPath, gapId, moduleId and note to the resolution store untyped; a number or object becomes a scope key.

## Description
src/app/api/gdd-compliance/route.ts:26 `body.projectPath ?? ''`, :35 `if (!body.gapId)` - `gapId: 5` or `projectPath: {}` reach resolveGap/listResolutions. Resolutions are scoped by project (docblock :13-15), so a non-string scope silently writes under a key no reader asks for. Fixed = typeof string checks with 400s.

## Flow
- POST {action:"resolve-gap", gapId: 5, projectPath: {}} -> 200 or a SQLite bind error 500
- add checks; test

## Expected impact
Triage writes always land in a readable scope. No in-tree caller sends non-strings.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - scope keys are strings
Before: 4 fields unchecked
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - code read; not probed
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test with numeric gapId and object projectPath

title: batch-review defaults ueVersion to 5.5 while the project is on UE 5.8
body:
## Summary
When the client omits ueVersion, every batch-review prompt tells the agent the project is UE 5.5.

## Description
src/app/api/feature-matrix/batch-review/route.ts:152 `const ueVersion = body.ueVersion || '5.5'`. The UE project was upgraded to 5.8 (2026-06-18); Both in-tree callers send it (src/hooks/useBatchReview.ts:84, src/lib/evaluator/review-runner.ts:246, which requires --ue-version), so the literal only reaches out-of-tree/MCP callers - low impact, but a stale literal. A stale engine version in the prompt steers reviews toward deprecated APIs. Fixed = no hardcoded default: take it from the project store/context the same way buildProjectContextHeader does, or refuse a missing ueVersion.

## Flow
- POST batch-review without ueVersion -> prompt ctx {ueVersion:"5.5"}
- trace where review-runner builds its body
- replace the literal with the shared source

## Expected impact
Reviews judge against the right engine. Needs the shared source of the version identified.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one source of truth for the engine version
Before: 1 hardcoded "5.5" default in the route
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - read; review-runner body not traced
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: batch-review test asserting the prompt ctx ueVersion for a body without one

title: game-design-doc POST passes a non-string projectName into the synthesized GDD
body:
## Summary
POST {action:"generate"} uses `body.projectName ?? 'Untitled Project'` without a type check, so a number/object becomes the document title.

## Description
src/app/api/game-design-doc/route.ts:82; the GET twin reads a query string (always string). `projectName: {}` renders "[object Object]" into the title and the markdown/pitch exports. Fixed = `typeof === "string" && trim()` else default.

## Flow
- POST {action:"generate", projectName:{}} -> title "[object Object]"
- fix + test

## Expected impact
Cosmetic correctness of exports; no caller sends non-strings today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - title is always a string
Before: 1 unchecked field
After: 0
Method: simulation - read
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: route test with object projectName asserting the default title

title: Decide the API range for combat tuning multipliers (UI 0.5-2.0, API unbounded)
body:
## Summary
Tuning multipliers are now required to be finite (0c083ded) but have no range; 1e9 health is accepted and simulated.

## Description
src/types/combat-simulator.ts:82-89 documents each multiplier as 0.5-2.0 (the slider range) and src/app/api/combat-simulator/route.ts clamps config fields but not tuning. Probe: playerHealthMul 1e9 -> 200, avgPlayerHealthRemaining 1.58e11. Whether scripted/MCP callers may explore beyond the slider range is a product call: clamp, refuse, or allow-and-flag.

## Flow
- operator picks clamp / refuse / allow
- implement in resolveTuning with a test

## Expected impact
Prevents nonsense balance verdicts from out-of-range sweeps, or deliberately permits them.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - API range policy for tuning
Before: unbounded
After: depends on the decision
Method: probe - 1e9 accepted; the target is a decision, not a figure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: operator decision on the allowed range
